patch.value: Post-merge guidance names history-repair, which clears drift but never settles the merge receipt, so every merged item leaves a permanent merge_decisions_unreviewed warning

Reproduced end to end in a sandbox repo with two agent branches editing the same item. The field-aware merge itself is excellent: status from theirs, priority from ours, tags unioned, both comments preserved, zero conflict markers. The problem is entirely in what an agent is told to do next.

After the merge the driver prints: 'The merged history chain was re-anchored. Run "pm validate --check-history-drift" and "pm history-repair --all" after the merge to reconcile item state with merged history.' (src/sdk/merge/driver.ts:280). The same command is named at src/sdk/merge/install.ts:702, wired into the health remediation map at src/sdk/governance/health.ts:2694, and documented in docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md:215 and docs/COMMANDS.md:830. Not one of those five sites mentions pm merge reconcile.

Following that guidance verbatim produces:

  pm history-repair --all      -> totals.repaired: 1
  pm validate --check-history-drift -> ok: true, has_warnings: false, drifted_items_count: 0
  pm health --check-only       -> warnings: [merge_decisions_unreviewed:1]     <-- still there
  pm validate                  -> warnings: [validate_merge_decisions_unreviewed:1]
  pm merge report              -> receipt state: "pending"

Only pm merge reconcile settles the receipt; after it, health is clean. So the two repair paths are not equivalent and the guidance names the one that cannot finish the job. history-repair re-anchors the chain, which is why the drift check goes green and an agent reasonably concludes the merge is fully reconciled - the strongest available signal says so.

The cost is unbounded and accrues exactly where the project most wants to be trustworthy. Each merged item leaves one permanent pending receipt, so a team of agents merging branches accumulates warnings forever, on every pm health and pm validate, with no natural point at which anyone clears them. Warning noise of that shape trains agents to ignore the warning channel, which is where genuine merge corruption would also surface. pm-ysqb6n (GH-770) closed by making pending receipts visible to validation and CI; that visibility is what makes this leak permanent rather than silent, so the two are complementary rather than duplicates.

Fix direction, in order of preference: (a) make history-repair settle receipts for streams it re-anchors, or refuse and redirect when a pending receipt covers the stream; (b) correct the remediation text at all five sites to name pm merge reconcile as the post-merge entry point, with history-repair as the narrower drift-only tool; (c) have pm merge reconcile be what the driver, install hint, and health remediation map all point at. Relates to pm-ei6x66 (no git hooks are installed, so nothing runs reconcile automatically) - reconcile's own guidance says 'No Git hook is installed automatically; invoke this command from an explicit post-merge hook only when your repository policy opts in.'
Following the remediation text the merge driver and pm health emit returns the workspace to zero warnings; no path clears history drift while leaving a receipt pending

message: Typed lineage: receipt visibility from GH-770 is what makes this leak permanent; no hook runs reconcile

value.text:
Remediation text is part of the product's contract with agents, and it can be wrong in a way tests never catch: every assertion here passes, because each individual command does what its own tests say. The defect only exists in the composition — follow the printed guidance to the letter, then check whether the system reports itself clean. It did not.

Worth generalizing into a habit: after any operation that prints "run X next", run X and then re-run the full diagnostic. The gap between "the remediation succeeded" and "the workspace is clean" is where this class lives, and drift-clean-but-receipt-pending is invisible unless both are checked.

value.text: Receipt scope evidence (2026-08-02). The merge receipt is not only unsettled, it is the sole record of what a merge destroyed: for a scalar conflict it carries retained_hash and discarded_hash and no values, so once the driver stdout is gone there is no way to recover or even read the losing value. Two clones merging the same branch pair in opposite directions produce opposite receipts, both validate clean afterwards, and nothing joins the two. See pm-dlx7v7.
